asks.title: Signing the new app (when you want a signed build)
asks.note: 1. Join the Apple Developer Program and note the Team ID (developer.apple.com, Membership). 2. On your Mac, make a Developer ID Application certificate (Xcode, Settings, Accounts, Manage Certificates, +). 3. Export it from Keychain Access as a .p12 with a password. 4. Make an app-specific password at appleid.apple.com. 5. Add CSC_LINK (the .p12 in base64), CSC_KEY_PASSWORD, APPLE_ID, APPLE_TEAM_ID and APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD as repository secrets on wsp-labs/wsp; today's release already reads these names. 6. Keep the bundle id wsp.desktop.experimental or name another. 7. Run the build script with them set. Until then the build is unsigned, which is fine for your own Mac.

asks.title: A host bug for the main lane
asks.note: After a commit or discard, the host can briefly report the old checkout state: a fresh read can be answered by one already in flight (packages/runtime/src/machines/reach.ts:389). Today's app has it too. It is runtime code, so it was left alone here.

json.leak: During one of Settings' test runs, a helper agent's tool printed its whole environment. That put two token values into that helper's conversation on its cloud machine: GH_TOKEN, the GitHub token the cloud machines push with, and WSP_HOST_TOKEN, the token that lets that thread talk to your wsp host. A Claude Code messaging token went with them. They did not reach a file, a log or the thread history this host keeps (I checked: the names don't appear there). They did go to the model with that conversation, and they sit in its session files on that cloud machine until it is deleted. Low risk, but the clean fix is to rotate GH_TOKEN in GitHub and to restart or re-key the host token. Builders now have a rule and a hand-in check against printing the environment.
